feedback.problem: Find the mass of an ice object which has the form of a quarter-disk, in the fourth quadrant, of radius $3$ centered at the origin and mass density function $\lambda $ given by $\lambda (x,y)=8({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})$
feedback.worked_solution:
The mass of a quarter-disk $D$ of radius $3$ centered at the origin with mass density $\lambda (x,y)=8({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}8({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }\lambda (r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

First, let's sketch our region $D:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14066271/assets/4f7b1647d893512605ee1a2e9cee3e5511a00dc7ad9b1765fff1d0ba0710895f.png)

In polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 3,\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le 0}.
$$

Finally, using the change of variables formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}8({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}8({r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{3}8{r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =8{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}[\frac{{r}^{4}}{4}]_{0}^{3}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}(81-0)\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =162{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =162[\theta ]_{-\pi /2}^{0} \\  & =162(0-(-\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & =81\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the total mass of the quarter-disk is $M=81\pi .$
